ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows two intersecting circular boundaries, one larger circle on the left and one smaller circle on the right; the two circles overlap to form a lens-shaped region in the middle. Therefore the space inside the circles is divided into the part unique to the left circle, the overlapping part, and the part unique to the right circle, 3 pieces in total. Then reason: Change the problem into two intersecting squares. First draw the first square; its interior has only 1 region. In order to make the number of regions the greatest, the second square should be placed so that its boundary intersects the boundary of the first square as many times as possible. One side of a square is a line segment, and it can intersect the boundary of another convex square at most 2 times; the second square has 4 sides, so there can be at most 4×2=8 intersection points. This can be achieved by appropriately rotating and overlapping the two squares. Along the boundary of the second square, each time it passes through an existing boundary, one more region will be cut out, so on the basis of the original 1 region, at most 8 regions can be added. The total number is 1+8=9. Final answer: 9
